title: How Much Does Salesforce Cost? CRM Pricing by Edition
summary: Salesforce pricing starts at $25 per user monthly, scaling to $500+ based on plan tier. Review each tier to estimate your actual spend.
body_markdown:
## Salesforce integration work with Activepieces


When the expensive part is custom syncing between Salesforce and your billing, support or marketing tools, Activepieces, whose MIT-licensed core ships with 746 integrations, can take it over, and that's the part of the integration budget it touches.


It's an automation tool where you build workflows by connecting steps on a canvas instead of writing code. It doesn't touch the licence bill or the limits behind it.


### What it can take off the integration budget


Look at custom syncing first, because that is where implementation money tends to go. Someone writes code that watches for a change in Salesforce, passes it to another system, and then has to be paid again whenever either side changes.


To cover this, Activepieces has a large, growing integration catalogue, and flows start from triggers and run deterministic steps. If an integration is missing, a team can generate one with AI and add it privately to its own instance.


You wire those to the other tool in a visual workflow, and a person who doesn't write code can maintain it.


One such flow is shown in the screenshot below. A failed payment in Stripe, a payment processor, starts a run, and a Slack message goes to a channel with the failure details, all for 1 credit.


In the run details on the left, the step completed in well under a second, and the notice at the bottom confirms it succeeded.


Swap Salesforce in as the trigger or the destination and you have the same pattern: a billing event updates an account, or a case change alerts the team that owns it.


What follows from that is practical. Work you'd have scoped as a custom build becomes a workflow you can inspect, rerun and change yourself, so the next small request costs you an afternoon instead of a new quote.


### What it doesn't change


Activepieces counts the run, not the steps inside it: 1 credit per flow run, so a ten-step Salesforce sync costs the same as the two-step workaround it replaced.


Splitting the work into smaller steps never raises that bill, but every read or write still counts against your edition's API call allowance.


Build workflows around the triggers that fire on a change instead of polling, and count the calls before you launch.


Nor does the per-user licence price change. If your edition lacks a feature you need, or your data and API caps are too low, a workflow tool won't raise them.


It lowers one line of the bill, implementation, and leaves the rest where it was. That's a narrow fit, but for teams paying developers to keep syncs alive, it's a real one.
